original_card.question: Can one known scalar simplification be converted into an actual paid-profile improvement?
methods: Derive the changed legal frame itinerary and exact child histogram.
Prove a scoped obstruction showing why that scalar gain cannot change the paid contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An unchanged histogram is not a kappa gain; record any separate runtime or proof benefit explicitly.

first_step.inspect: Observe that the positive control improves scalar counts while retaining the paid histogram.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one simplification and derive the complete changed frame itinerary, or prove why it cannot change the histogram.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legal change to the histogram, not addition count alone, is the bridge to an exponent gain.
allowed_variations: One existing scalar simplification and one proposed frame-path change.
scope_change_triggers: Submitting only another scalar count as completion of a paid-profile task.

actual_scope: One exact scalar re-delivery (a seven-insert helper-donor kernel for cold pivot 566) on the two local words of the highest open construction (PR1297 words in PR1319's T74 exact fill), converted into a changed legal frame itinerary and child histogram: per call H1 +1, H2 -2, H3 +1 on both words, with unchanged interfaces, owners, dispatch and idle remainder; priced through PR1319's complete strict T74 admission chain and, stacked, through PR1549's 200-digit refined assembler.
scope_change_reason: The card names a known scalar simplification on the selected record; the useful instance is on the highest open construction (PR1319, refined by PR1377...PR1549), whose two local words are byte-identical to PR1297's. The simplification is a new exact helper-donor kernel found by an all-pivot slot-screened search, not a pre-existing scalar count.
bottleneck_link: The binding supplier is complex; a legal histogram change of the local words moves the complex moment endpoint and hence kappa at fixed owners: +4.14e-8 here, against the ~1e-21 steps of the concurrent precision refinements.
stop_rule: Stop after one admitted paid-profile gain on the frontier words, or after the slot-screened pivot families are exhausted.
evidence: evidence/STRICT-T74.json (PASS_STRICT_MIXED_T74_EXACT_FILL, kappa 0.001676896669021299), evidence/REFINED-R200.json (PR1549 refined assembler), evidence/REBUILD.json, evidence/NATIVE.json, evidence/PRICING.json; bounded replay verify.py, full replay replay_full.py.
author: Marius-Paul Dumitrean
ai_assistance: Substantial: Anthropic Claude (via Claude Code) ran the searches, wrote the scripts and drafted the text under the author's direction; results were re-checked by this package's scripts and unchanged predecessor code.

open_questions.question: Do other written cold pivots admit kernels of this seven-insert shape (helper window restored after the pivot's own early-cleanup restoration, plus donor windows)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Each such kernel is a mass-neutral paid-profile gain worth roughly 4e-8 kappa at T74; the four PR1297 kernels and this one share the copy-and-restore pivot structure.
open_questions.first_step: Run the slot-screened search on the 197 pivots not yet covered (the 81 searched included 566; screens of 506/518/554 were negative at -6,780 under base caps but unrealized).
open_questions.blocked_by: Most single-read slots are frame-infeasible because of fixed end frames (perp(port), helper_final); larger compensations need joint slot feasibility.

open_questions.question: Can the never-written copy-window pivots (439/444/438/440 and the -51,648 group) gain with edits that also re-time port-chain gates (a two-column identity)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Their uncompensated deletion screens are 3-4x larger (-51k to -68k per call) than this kernel.
open_questions.first_step: Move one conflicting port gate (e.g. B510 past B834 with a compensating 190 += -381) and re-solve the q-compensation with the cleanup-prepend route.
open_questions.blocked_by: Insert-only, window, partial-deletion, tail-undo and single port-retime families are all neutral or infeasible on these words.

open_questions.question: Does the kernel survive an independent cold rebuild of the frames (re-deriving the exact optimal frames rather than shipping them)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The shipped words carry solver-derived frames that audit_local and the native chain validate, but the frame optimum itself is reproduced only with the PR1186 toolkit.
open_questions.first_step: Re-solve the frames of the edited scalar program with the PR1186 toolkit or an independent solver and compare profiles.
open_questions.blocked_by: PR1186 is not merged; an independent frame solver does not exist yet.
